archetypes.name: parity-drift
archetypes.rationale: The plan makes repeated parity claims against specific bash scripts but never exhaustively compares its Python descriptions to those scripts; unacknowledged divergences will cause silent behavioral drift that the static panel won't catch without reading the shell sources.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read the three shell references named in the issue (lint-fix-loop.sh, run-relevant-checks-captured.sh, and the run_checks_phase logic in ship-pr.sh) and compare their actual behavior line-by-line to what the plan describes. Specifically hunt for discrepancies in: the attempt-counter initialization and increment order in the fixer loop; the two-consecutive-empty-failure rule and exactly what the bash counts as 'empty'; the forbidden-path reversion sequence (committed delta vs. working-tree, ordering of reset vs. checkout vs. rm); the exact argv passed to scripts/git-commit.sh and the commit-message template; and the log-marker strings the plan uses to parse coverage and phase. The plan acknowledges one known divergence (fixer tier order vs. config.FIXER_TIER_ORDER) but presents it as a deliberate choice — verify the rationale holds and flag any other unacknowledged divergences. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: sibling-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan assumes specific exported symbols, type signatures, and call semantics from Phase 1+ sibling modules but never cross-checks them against what those modules actually export; any mismatch is a silent import-time or runtime failure invisible to the static panel.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read each sibling Python module the plan imports — proc.py, agents.py, outcomes.py, redact.py, git.py, errors.py, config.py — and verify that every symbol the plan calls or references (Runner, classify_launch_failure, is_transient_infra_failure, TierAttempt, run_waterfall, Outcome, StepResult, redact, rev_parse, status, reset, RCC_MAX_ITER_DEFAULT, FIXER_TIER_ORDER) is actually present, exported, and carries a compatible signature. Pay special attention to whether StepResult accepts a payload keyword argument, whether outcomes.Outcome is an enum or a plain class, whether agents.run_waterfall exists at all or whether its short-circuit semantics match the plan's claim that they are CI-specific, and whether git.py's existing verbs accept the argument shapes the plan assumes for rev_parse and reset. Flag any symbol that is absent, renamed, or typed differently from what the plan assumes. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
